insights.title: Your LDL cholesterol is in the severe range
insights.found: LDL cholesterol 196 mg/dL (5.1 mmol/L) on 10 Oct 2026, and you take no cholesterol medicine.
insights.why: Our rules flag LDL in the severe-hypercholesterolaemia range and at the high-lifetime-risk level, with South Asian ancestry as a guideline-named risk enhancer.
insights.means: At this level guidelines ask doctors to consider an inherited cause (familial hypercholesterolaemia), to check close relatives, and to involve a lipid specialist, after first ruling out other causes such as an underactive thyroid, kidney protein loss or liver bile problems.
insights.do: Repeat a fasting lipid test within 2 weeks to 6 months, then have a risk discussion with your doctor. Starting a medicine is your doctor's decision.
insights.expected: A confirmed result leads to a clear plan, and possibly testing for your family.
insights.helps: The single biggest lever on your heart risk.

insights.title: Your ApoB and Lp(a) are both high
insights.found: ApoB 142 mg/dL and Lp(a) 78 mg/dL on 10 Oct 2026.
insights.why: ApoB is above the high-lifetime-risk level, and Lp(a) is at or above the 50 mg/dL risk-enhancing threshold.
insights.means: In South Asian patients ApoB can show more risk than LDL; where the two disagree it is the more informative measure. Lp(a) is mostly inherited and is measured once in a lifetime; there is no treatment threshold, so it is read with your overall risk.
insights.do: Repeat ApoB with your lipid test within 2 to 8 weeks. Your Lp(a) does not need repeating.
insights.expected: Your doctor weighs both in the risk discussion.

insights.title: Your blood pressure reading was 156
insights.found: Office systolic blood pressure 156 mmHg on 10 Oct 2026. You take amlodipine.
insights.why: Our rule flags a systolic reading of 140 or more.
insights.means: One office reading does not diagnose anything. Repeated readings, preferably outside the clinic, show your usual level.
insights.do: Take repeat readings within 1 to 8 weeks, at home if you can.
insights.expected: Your doctor sees whether your treatment is enough.

insights.title: Your record flags you as a current smoker
insights.found: Your record carries the flag 'current smoker'.
insights.why: Smoking is one of the inputs heart-risk models use; no rule in our library grades it on its own.
insights.means: With your cholesterol and blood pressure, smoking adds to the same arteries' load.
insights.do: If you would like to stop, ask your doctor about support.
insights.expected: Stopping is something you can start today.

insights.title: Your waist, weight, triglycerides and HDL form a pattern
insights.found: Waist 96 cm, BMI 26.2, triglycerides 210 mg/dL and HDL 34 mg/dL on 10 Oct 2026.
insights.why: Waist is above the Asian-Indian cut-point for men (90 cm), BMI above the WHO Asian action point (23), triglycerides at or above 175, and HDL below 40.
insights.means: These are metabolic-syndrome factors. In a 10-year Indian cohort, a waist above the cut-point carried about twice the risk of diabetes, high blood pressure and heart disease. Triglycerides count only if a second fasting test is also high.
insights.do: Repeat triglycerides within 2 weeks to 3 months; recheck waist in 6 to 12 months.
insights.expected: A smaller waist usually moves several of these numbers together.

insights.title: Your inflammation marker is raised
insights.why: It is at or above 2.0 mg/L, the entry level used in the JUPITER trial.
insights.means: After our ancestry adjustment this is informational: one value cannot show lasting inflammation, and any recent infection makes it unreliable.
insights.do: Nothing to do now; it can be repeated in a year or two.
insights.expected: Context for your doctor's risk discussion.

insights.title: Your eGFR may slightly overestimate your kidney function
insights.why: In Indian cohorts, creatinine-based equations overestimate true kidney function in the 60-89 band.
insights.means: Your kidney function is probably fine, but the number may be a little high. Urine albumin has not been measured.
insights.do: Add urine albumin to your panel; cystatin C if your doctor wants a second marker.

ask.q: Could my high cholesterol run in the family?
ask.a: At this LDL level guidelines ask doctors to consider familial hypercholesterolaemia and to check close relatives, after ruling out other causes. Your family history was not in your record; adding it helps.
That is your doctor's decision; our analysis does not prescribe. Our rules say: confirm LDL on a repeat fasting sample, then hold a risk discussion.

A cholesterol particle whose level is mostly inherited. Yours is 78 mg/dL, at or above the 50 mg/dL risk-enhancing level. It is measured once in a lifetime and read with your overall risk; there is no treatment threshold.

ask.q: Is my blood pressure too high?
ask.a: One office reading was 156 systolic while you take amlodipine. Repeat readings over the next 1 to 8 weeks, ideally at home, show your usual level.

ask.q: Does smoking matter with these results?
ask.a: Your record flags you as a current smoker. It is an input to heart-risk models and adds to the same arteries as your cholesterol and blood pressure. Your doctor can help if you want to stop.

Not calculated: the PREVENT model needs total cholesterol, HDL, treatment status, diabetes status, smoking and BMI recorded in the form it reads, and the run did not have them all. We never fill gaps with guesses.
hs-CRP was 3.6 mg/L. One value cannot show lasting inflammation, and any recent infection makes it unreliable. Our rule treats it as information only.
Not calculated. PhenoAge needs nine blood results; 7 are missing: albumin, CRP, lymphocyte %, MCV, RDW, alkaline phosphatase and white cell count.

glossary: Two kinds of cholesterol in the blood. LDL is the main one linked to clogged arteries; HDL is often called 'good' cholesterol.
A count of the particles that carry cholesterol into artery walls.
Lipoprotein(a): a cholesterol particle whose level is mostly inherited; measured once in a lifetime.
A type of fat in the blood, measured after fasting.
High-sensitivity C-reactive protein: a blood marker of inflammation.
Waist circumference: a measure of fat around the middle.
Body mass index: weight divided by height squared.
Estimated glomerular filtration rate: how well your kidneys filter, calculated from creatinine, age and sex.
One of our clinical checks. Each has a source, a threshold and an evidence grade; it fires only when your result clears it.
panel_prep: One morning visit in the next few weeks.
Fast for 10-12 hours before (water is fine).
Avoid the visit within two weeks of an infection, which can upset CRP.
Bring a list of your medicines.

genes.function: Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork together with laminins, proteoglycans and entactin/nidogen.
PPIase that catalyzes the cis-trans isomerization of proline imidic peptide bonds in oligopeptides and may therefore assist protein folding.

Metabolic-stress sensing protein kinase that phosphorylates the alpha subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (EIF2S1/eIF-2-alpha) in response to various stress, such as unfolded protein response (UPR).
Deacetylates a wide range of non-histone substrates.
Electrogenic Na(+)-coupled sugar symporter that actively transports D-glucose at the plasma membrane, with a Na(+) to sugar coupling ratio of 1:1.
Receptor for both mineralocorticoids (MC) such as aldosterone and glucocorticoids (GC) such as corticosterone or cortisol.
Receptor for angiotensin II, a vasoconstricting peptide, which acts as a key regulator of blood pressure and sodium retention by the kidney.
